university.label: Students still waiting for a grade
Per department: courses offered + average credits
university.sql:
SELECT DeptName, count(*), avg(Credits)
FROM course
GROUP BY DeptName
ORDER BY avg(Credits) DESC, DeptName;

university.label: Per student: courses taken vs passed
university.note: count(Grade) skips NULLs; that asymmetry is the whole trick.

university.label: Courses above their department's average credits
university.sql:
SELECT CourseID, Title, Credits
FROM course AS c1
WHERE credits > (SELECT avg(c2.Credits)
    FROM course AS c2
    WHERE c2.DeptName = c1.DeptName);
university.note: The correlated subquery, week 3's boss fight (the notebook kept two wrong attempts above it).

university.label: Courses with no prerequisites
university.sql:
SELECT CourseID, Title
FROM course
WHERE CourseID NOT IN (
    SELECT CourseID
    FROM Prereq);

university.label: Students who never enrolled in anything
university.sql:
SELECT StudName
FROM student

university.label: Instructors who taught in spring 2009
Who taught the most sections in spring 2009
university.sql:
SELECT InstID, InstName, count(*)
FROM instructor NATURAL JOIN Teaches
WHERE Semester = 'Spring' AND StudyYear = '2009'
GROUP BY InstID
HAVING count(*) >= (
    SELECT max(cnt) FROM (
        SELECT count(*) AS cnt
        FROM instructor NATURAL JOIN Teaches
        WHERE Semester = 'Spring' AND StudyYear = '2009'
        GROUP BY InstID));
university.original:
Select InstID, InstName, Count(*)
From instructor natural join Teaches
 where Semester = 'Spring' and StudyYear = '2009'
 group by InstID
having count(*) >= ALL (Select  Count(*)
	From instructor natural join Teaches
	where Semester = 'Spring' and StudyYear = '2009'
	group by InstID);
university.note: Adapted: SQLite has no quantified >= ALL, so the inner counts collapse to max().

university.label: Least-taken spring 2009 courses (zero students count too)
university.sql:
SELECT CourseID, Title, count(StudID)
FROM course NATURAL JOIN section NATURAL LEFT JOIN takes
WHERE semester = 'Spring' AND StudyYear = 2009
GROUP BY CourseID
HAVING count(StudID) <= (
    SELECT min(cnt) FROM (
        SELECT count(StudID) AS cnt
        FROM section NATURAL LEFT JOIN takes
        WHERE semester = 'Spring' AND StudyYear = 2009
        GROUP BY CourseID));
university.original:
Select CourseID, Title, Count(StudID)
From course natural join section natural left join takes
where semester = "Spring" and StudyYear=2009
group by CourseID
having count(StudID) <= all (Select Count(StudID)
	From section natural left join takes
	where semester = "Spring" and StudyYear=2009
    group by CourseID);
university.note: Adapted: <= ALL becomes min(); the natural LEFT join keeps courses nobody took.

university.label: Students taking more courses than average
university.sql:
WITH courseTaken(StudID, NumCourses) AS (
    SELECT StudID, count(CourseID)
    FROM student NATURAL LEFT JOIN takes
    GROUP BY StudID)
SELECT StudID, StudName
FROM student NATURAL JOIN courseTaken
WHERE NumCourses > (SELECT avg(NumCourses) FROM courseTaken);
university.note: Adapted: the original's CREATE VIEW becomes a CTE so the preset leaves no state behind.

cinema.label: 1.1 Tickets over 120 DKK
1.2 Tickets to Sci-Fi movies
cinema.note: Quoting adapted: MariaDB lets strings live in double quotes, SQLite prefers single.

cinema.label: 1.3 Sci-Fi tickets for movies never shown in Ruby
cinema.sql:
SELECT tid
FROM ticket NATURAL JOIN projection NATURAL JOIN movie NATURAL JOIN room
WHERE genre = 'Sci-Fi' AND mid NOT IN (
    SELECT mid FROM projection NATURAL JOIN room WHERE rname = 'Ruby');

cinema.label: 2.1 Income per movie
2.2 Movies earning above the average
cinema.sql:
WITH incomeview AS (
    SELECT mid, title, genre, sum(price) AS income
    FROM movie NATURAL JOIN projection NATURAL JOIN ticket
    GROUP BY mid)
SELECT mid, title, genre, income
FROM incomeview
WHERE income > (SELECT avg(income) FROM incomeview);
cinema.note: Adapted: the original parked the average in a MariaDB session variable (@aveinc); a CTE + subquery does it statelessly.

cinema.label: 2.3 Movies at or above their genre's average income
cinema.sql:
WITH incomeview AS (
    SELECT mid, title, genre, sum(price) AS income
    FROM movie NATURAL JOIN projection NATURAL JOIN ticket
    GROUP BY mid)
SELECT mid, title, genre, income
FROM incomeview AS i1
WHERE income >= (SELECT avg(income) FROM incomeview AS i2 WHERE i1.genre = i2.genre);

cinema.label: 3.2 Reserved seats per room on Dec 19
cinema.sql:
SELECT rid, (
    SELECT count(tid)
    FROM projection AS p2 NATURAL JOIN ticket
    WHERE p2.rid = p1.rid AND p2.pdate = p1.pdate) AS reserved_seats
FROM projection AS p1 WHERE pdate = '2025-12-19';
cinema.note: Adapted: the original defined a MariaDB stored function reservedSeats(rid, pdate); SQLite has no stored functions, so it inlines as a correlated subquery.

cinema.label: 3.3 Empty seats per projection
cinema.sql:
SELECT pid, count(sno) - (
    SELECT count(tid)
    FROM projection AS p2 NATURAL JOIN ticket
    WHERE p2.rid = p1.rid AND p2.pdate = p1.pdate) AS empty_seats
FROM projection AS p1 NATURAL JOIN seat
GROUP BY pid;

takeaway.label: 2.2 Items never ordered by Peter Pan
takeaway.sql:
SELECT itemId, description FROM foodItem
WHERE itemId NOT IN (SELECT itemId
    FROM orderline NATURAL JOIN foodOrder NATURAL JOIN customer
    WHERE name = 'Peter Pan');

takeaway.label: 2.3 ... more than once
takeaway.sql:
SELECT itemId, description FROM foodItem
WHERE itemId NOT IN (SELECT itemId
    FROM orderline NATURAL JOIN foodOrder NATURAL JOIN customer
    WHERE name = 'Peter Pan'
    GROUP BY itemId, custNo
    HAVING count(*) > 1);

takeaway.label: 3.3 Total spend per customer
takeaway.sql:
SELECT custNo, (
    SELECT sum(unitPrice * quantity)
    FROM FoodOrder NATURAL JOIN Orderline
    WHERE custNo = Customer.custNo) AS total_cost
FROM Customer;
takeaway.note: Adapted: the MariaDB stored function inlines as a correlated subquery.
